title: Shooting a laser at the Galactic Centre
caption: A laser aimed at the Galactic Centre from Yepun, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A laser beam shoots out of Yepun, Unit Telescope 4 of ESO's Very Large Telescope, pointing straight at the centre of our galaxy. Behind the 8.2-metre telescope spreads the Milky Way, a sweep of countless stars and dust. The view is very wide, spanning about 180 degrees, and on the right stands one of the 1.8-metre Auxiliary Telescopes, which are used for interferometry.
The beam creates an artificial star. Working with the adaptive optics system, it lets the telescope record images and spectra free of the blurring that Earth's atmosphere normally adds.

ESO astronomer Yuri Beletsky took the picture on 10 May 2010. At that moment, the SINFONI instrument and the laser guide star facility were in use by astronomers Stefan Gillessen and Hauke Enkel, who were studying the Milky Way's centre, home to a lurking supermassive black hole.

understand.summary: This is a very wide-angle ground-based photograph by Yuri Beletsky, covering about 180 degrees; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The camera takes in a far wider sweep of sky at once than the eye, and it may record the Milky Way's dust and stars more vividly too.
